candidate_047.name: repair-vs-fresh-restart arbitration / anchoring-aware repair
candidate_047.mechanism: When a branch fails, compare targeted repair of the existing trajectory against a fresh restart/resample under matched remaining budget. Prefer repair only when the retained trajectory carries demonstrably useful information and anchoring/near-copy risk is acceptably low; otherwise restart or branch fresh. Record the chosen counterfactual and budget so improvement is not misattributed to feedback rather than simply receiving another attempt.
candidate_047.positive_or_negative_evidence: cross-domain negative/causal control from code agents
candidate_047.source: arXiv:2607.26117, Try Again, Don't Look Back: Blind Resampling Outperforms Self-Repair in Small Code Models, 2026-07-28
candidate_047.quantitative_evidence: Placebo-controlled MBPP+ study across 1.5B/3B/7B models compared matched-budget blind resampling, content-free failure notice, execution feedback, and feedback+reflection. Blind resampling was strongest below 7B and tied best at 7B while using 2.5-5.5x fewer tokens; conditioning on the model's failed attempt cost 6.1 points at 1.5B (p=0.006). Near-identical retries occurred 33-68% with self-repair versus 2-14% under blind resampling. The penalty replicated across an independent model family/precision and correlated with baseline quality r=0.96.
candidate_047.scope_guard: Code-generation evidence only. It does not establish that fresh restart beats repair in autonomous science; it falsifies the assumption that feedback-conditioned repair should be credited without a matched fresh-retry control and motivates a science-domain repair-versus-restart arbitration experiment.
